question.prompt: How many positive three-digit integers have a remainder of \(2\) when divided by \(6,\) a remainder of \(5\) when divided by \(9,\) and a remainder of \(7\) when divided by \(11?\)

solutions.explanation:
Each stated remainder is four less than its divisor. Thus if the integer is \(n\), adding \(4\) makes it divisible by \(6\), \(9\), and \(11\) all at once.

Their least common multiple is \(2\cdot3^2\cdot11=198\), so \(n+4=198k\) for an integer \(k\). Conversely, subtracting \(4\) from any multiple of \(198\) gives the required remainders \(2,5,7\), so this description includes exactly the solutions.

The three-digit condition gives

\[
100\leq198k-4\leq999,
\]

or \(104\leq198k\leq1003\). Hence \(k=1,2,3,4,5\), producing

\[
194,392,590,788,986.
\]

There are \(\boxed{5}\) integers, choice \(\boxed{\text{E}}\). A common shortfall from each divisor suggests adding that amount before taking a least common multiple.
solutions.title: Add4 to turn all three remainder conditions into divisibility
